lines: A clock generator whose rate is multiplied by any of sixteen ratios you switch on, with a scan control picking one of them and further outputs for the lowest, highest and middlemost
Sets the clock rate from 1 to 700 bpm, and is ignored while a cable is patched to the rate input
Holds the phase at zero for as long as it is held down, and sends 10V from the reset output meanwhile
Reads the rate input as a 0-10V phasor rather than as clock pulses while it is lit, which locks to whatever drives it with no delay; unlit, that input needs two pulses before a rate is known
Raises the phase to this power before any ratio is applied, 0.11 to 10: below 1 the cycle bunches towards its end, above 1 towards its start. A cable at the skew input replaces it
Divides 0 to 1 into as many regions as there are active ratios and picks the ratio whose region the setting falls in; the scan input's voltage is added to this knob before that choice is made
Pushes the start of the cycle back by this fraction of the ratio scan has chosen, 0 to 1, and is ignored while a cable is patched to the phase input
Adds this button's ratio to the list of active ratios while it is on; the scan, refl. scan, lowest, highest and middle outputs choose from that list and from nothing else
Sets the skew exponent in place of the knob while patched, 0-10V giving 0.11 to 10.11
Takes the clock this module runs from: rising edges above 1V with the phase button unlit, or a 0-10V phasor with it lit
Holds the phase at zero for as long as this reads above 0V
Adds to the scan knob, 0-10V covering the whole of that knob's travel, and the total is clamped to that travel
Sets the phase offset in place of the knob while patched, 0-10V covering the whole of that knob's travel
Turns its ratio on while this rises above 0.9V and off when it falls below 0.1V, and does nothing while that ratio's button is on, despite the tooltip calling it an inversion of the button
A 10V trigger at the start of each cycle of the clock, before any ratio is applied, and silent while reset is held
A 0-10V rising ramp, one per cycle of the clock, before any ratio or skew is applied
A 10V trigger each time the skewed phase multiplied by the ratio scan has chosen comes round to its start
A 0-10V rising ramp at the clock rate multiplied by the ratio scan has chosen, after skew
A 10V trigger each time the phase multiplied by the ratio at the mirror image of the scan setting comes round; scan at 0 gives the ratio scan at 1 would pick
A 0-10V rising ramp at the clock rate multiplied by the ratio at the mirror image of the scan setting, after skew
A 10V trigger each time the phase multiplied by the lowest active ratio comes round to its start
A 0-10V rising ramp at the clock rate multiplied by the lowest active ratio, after skew
A 10V trigger each time the phase multiplied by the highest active ratio comes round to its start
A 0-10V rising ramp at the clock rate multiplied by the highest active ratio, after skew
A 10V trigger each time the phase multiplied by the middlemost active ratio comes round; with an even number of active ratios the higher of the two middle ones is taken
A 0-10V rising ramp at the clock rate multiplied by the middlemost active ratio, after skew
Carries 10V for as long as the reset button is held or the reset input reads above 0V, and 0V the rest of the time
Note — every ratio multiplies the clock rate rather than dividing it, and they run from 1:1 up to 32:1, so a slow master clock gives the widest usable spread
Note — with no ratio button on at all, the module behaves as though a single 1:1 ratio were active and all six pairs of outputs run at the clock rate
Note — the ratio buttons and the phase offset are stored with the patch, but the rate, skew and scan knobs are ordinary parameters and come back where you left them
scanning_clock_multiplier_v2.notes: Written from the maker's source at commit 7f2d7f2 (the plugin.json that carries 2.0.1); no source file changed between that commit and the repository head, so head was read. The sixteen ratio gate inputs are configured with the tooltip 'inverts button value', which the code does not do: process() line 194 turns a ratio on when the button rises while the jack is low, or when the jack rises while the button is low, and off again on the matching falling edge, so a gate has no effect at all while the button for that ratio is on. The README describes the same behaviour and a 1V threshold; the Schmitt trigger in the code uses 0.9V rising and 0.1V falling. The rate input's Schmitt trigger is left at Rack's defaults, so the clock threshold there is 1V rising and 0V falling. Two inputs are configured with an empty name and so have no tooltip at all: the rate input and the reset input. The phase offset knob and the reset button are also configured with empty names. Index order is not panel order in the output section: the trig column reads 0, 3, 8, 9, 6, 11 down the panel and the phase column 2, 4, 5, 10, 7, 12.

lines: A tempo-driven function generator: it takes a 0-10V phasor or a clock and cuts one to sixteen envelopes out of every cycle of it, with controls that bend where in the cycle those envelopes fall
Reads the rate input as a 0-10V phasor while it is lit, following a change of rate at once; unlit, that input is read as a clock and two pulses are needed before a cycle length is known
Sets the attack of each envelope as a percentage of one hit's share of the cycle, 1 to 100 percent
Sets how far into each hit the envelope holds its full level, as a percentage of one hit's share of the cycle, 0 to 100 percent; that level is always the envelope's maximum
Sets how far into each hit the envelope reaches zero, as a percentage of one hit's share of the cycle, 1 to 100 percent
Bends the attack segment, 0 to 2: below 1 it rises fast and then slows, at 1 it is a straight line, above 1 it starts slowly. The display draws the envelope as though this were at 1
Bends the decay segment, 0 to 2: below 1 it falls fast and then slows, at 1 it is a straight line, above 1 it starts slowly. The display draws the envelope as though this were at 1
Sets how many envelopes are cut from each cycle, 1 to 16, or one of the other counts chosen from the menu
Sets where in the cycle the phase turns round, 0 to 1: at 1 it rises across the whole cycle, at 0.5 it rises over the first half and falls over the second, at 0 it falls across the whole cycle
Bends the phase before the envelopes are cut from it, so some envelopes are dwelt on and others passed through quickly; 1 is no bending, below 1 logarithmic and above 1 exponential
Reduces each envelope's height in proportion to how far through the cycle the phase has reached, from no reduction at 0 percent to complete at 100 percent
Takes the 0-10V phasor the envelopes are cut from, or a clock when the phase button is unlit
The signal multiplied by the envelope and sent to the vca output
Adds to the attack slider, 0-10V covering the whole of its travel
Adds to the sustain slider, 0-10V covering the whole of its travel
Adds to the decay slider, 0-10V covering the whole of its travel
Sets the number of hits in place of the knob while patched, 0-10V spread evenly over whichever counts the menu's hit count setting offers
Sets the turning point of the phase in place of the knob while patched, 0-10V giving 0 to 1
Sets the bending of the phase in place of the knob while patched, 0-10V giving 0 to 2
Scales how far the phase reduces the envelope's height, its 0-10V multiplied by the phase->env knob
The envelope, 0-10V, smoothed by a one-pole filter so that a sudden edge is rounded
The vca input multiplied by the envelope
Carries 10V through the whole attack segment of each envelope and for 1ms after it, rather than the short trigger at the start of the attack that the manual describes
The phase after skew and spread, 0-10V, which is the grey shape drawn on the display
Menu — Hit Count — a heading over four settings for what the hits knob steps through
Menu — 1-16 — the hits knob steps through every whole number from 1 to 16
Menu — 1 and powers of two — the hits knob steps through 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16
Menu — evens — the hits knob steps through 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14, although its top position prints as 16
Menu — multiples of 3 — the hits knob steps through 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15
Menu — rate input range — a heading over the two readings of the rate input
Menu — unipolar (0-10v) — reads one cycle at the rate input as 0V rising to 10V
Menu — bipolar(-5-5v) — adds half a cycle to the rate input, so one cycle is -5V rising to 5V
Note — nothing comes out until a phasor or a clock is patched to rate: with that jack empty the phase stays at zero, the env output stays at 0V and the trig output stays high at 10V
Note — the display is drawing only; no part of it responds to a click, and neither exp trimpot nor the phase->env knob is reflected in what it draws
Note — the hit count and the rate input range chosen from the menu are not saved with the patch, so both return to their first setting when a patch is reloaded
phase_driven_multihit_envelope.notes: Written from the maker's source at commit 7f2d7f2 (the plugin.json carrying 2.0.1); head carries the same source. Input 5 is declared in the enum as SPACE_INPUT and is the one input the worksheet lists as having no panel jack: there is no configInput for it and no addInput, so it cannot be clicked and it gets no line. Inputs 7 and 8, the skew and spread jacks, are configured with empty names and so have no tooltip. All four outputs are configured with empty names as well, so every output tooltip on this module is blank. The spread knob is configured 0 to 2.1 but process() clamps the value to 2.0, so the top five percent of that knob's travel does nothing; the same clamp on the two exp trimpots matches their configured range and costs nothing. The menu's 'evens' option labels the hits knob 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16 while the code computes 2 times the knob position, which gives 14 at the top; the label is wrong. Neither hitPattern nor the bipolar phase offset is written by dataToJson, so a patch reload restores the hits knob's 1-16 labelling and the unipolar rate reading whatever was chosen. In phase mode the leftover clock rate from a previous spell in clock mode is added to the phase every sample, so switching from clock to phase leaves the phase drifting until a reset of the patch.

lines: A polyphonic oscillator that gives its own pitch and three frequency-divided versions of that pitch at the same time, with through-zero FM and a choice of hard or windowed sync
Sets the pitch in volts, -5 to 5, added to the v/oct input; 0 gives C4 at 261.63Hz
Divides 0 to 1 into as many regions as there are active divisors and picks the divisor whose region the setting falls in; the scan input's voltage is added to this knob before that choice is made
Blends the wave across its travel from sine through triangle and saw to square
Sets how far the FM input moves the frequency, -2 to 2, with negative settings inverting it; the modulation is added to the frequency rather than multiplying it, so it passes through zero
Sets how deeply the window inverts the part of the wave inside it, and does nothing while the window button is unlit or the sync input is empty
Turns the sync input's plain hard sync into windowed sync while it is lit: the wave is multiplied by a window taken from the sync voltage, which softens the step that hard sync alone leaves
Adds this button's divisor to the list of active divisors while it is on; the scan, refl. and low outputs choose from that list and from nothing else
Adds to the scan knob, 0-10V covering the whole of that knob's travel
Sets the pitch at 1V per octave, added to the freq knob; the number of channels patched here is the number the module runs and the number every wave output carries
Adds to the sine-square knob, 0-10V covering the whole of that knob's travel, and the total is clamped to it
The signal that modulates the frequency, scaled by the depth knob and by the depth input
Scales the depth knob while patched, its 0-10V multiplied by that knob's setting
Resets all four of the module's phases on each rising edge; with the window button lit the wave is also multiplied by a window taken from this voltage
Turns its divisor on while this rises above 0.9V and off again when it falls below 0.1V, and has no effect while that divisor's button is already on
The wave at the pitch set by freq and v/oct, undivided, ±5V
The wave at the pitch set by freq and v/oct divided by the divisor scan has chosen, ±5V
The wave at the pitch divided by the divisor at the mirror image of the scan setting: scan at 0 gives what scan at 1 would pick
The wave at the pitch divided by the largest active divisor, which is the lowest pitch the module produces
A 10V trigger each time scan moves into a new region and the divisor it has chosen changes
Note — with no divisor button on at all, the scan, refl. and low outputs run at the undivided pitch that the freq output carries
Note — the channel count comes from the v/oct input alone; the sine-square input and the eight divisor gates are read on their first channel only, and the trig output is always one channel
Note — each channel is computed four times, once per wave output, so this oscillator costs more processor time than one that produces a single wave
scanning_frequency_division_osc_poly.notes: Written from the maker's source at commit 7f2d7f2 (the plugin.json carrying 2.0.1); head carries the same source. Thirteen of the fourteen inputs are configured with an empty name, so every input tooltip except the sine-square jack's is blank; the five outputs are all configured with empty names as well. Two polyphony faults are in the shipped code. In process(), the sync handling indexes engine.syncCheck[c+i] and engine.phase[c+i] with the absolute channel number rather than the lane number, so beyond the first four channels it reads and writes past the ends of a four-element array and a float_4; sync is correct on channels 1 to 4 only. In scanReturn(), the search index i is declared outside the loop over the four lanes and so is never reset between them, and the early return for a lane whose scan value falls in the first region returns that one divisor for all four lanes; with different scan voltages per channel the divisor chosen for the later channels can be wrong. The low output takes scanReturn at a scan value of 1, which is the largest active divisor and therefore the lowest pitch, matching what the README means by 'lowest'. The scan value fed to the divisor lookup is unclamped while the reflected scan value is clamped to 0 to 1; the lookup is bounded either way, so a scan input above 10V parks on the highest divisor.

lines: A polyphonic quantizer whose scale notes each carry a priority, giving four outputs of the same melody filtered to the whole scale, to a pentatonic, to a triad and to the root
Steps that note through five states: black keeps it out of every output, and dark grey, mid grey, light grey and white put it into prio1, into prio1 and prio2, into those and prio3, and into all four
Multiplies the input by -1 to 1, so it attenuates the signal and inverts it below zero; while a cable is patched to the gain input this knob attenuates that voltage instead
Adds -5V to 5V to the input after gain, and is ignored while a cable is patched to the offset input
Passes the held sample rather than the moment-to-moment input while it is lit; unlit, the input goes through unsampled and no sampling reaches the outputs
Sets how many of the shift register's sixteen steps are read before it returns to the first, 1 to 16; a shorter setting does not erase the steps past it
Plays the shift register to the outputs while it is lit, and writes the input into the register while it is unlit
Writes the input into the current step of the shift register while it is held, in place of playing that step back, and does nothing while the loop button is unlit
Chooses what a value below the floor becomes: to ceiling sends it to the ceiling, up oct adds 1V until it clears, rectify reflects it above the floor, clip sets it to the floor, bypass passes it
Chooses what a value above the ceiling becomes: to root sends it to a root note, down oct drops it 1V at a time, rectify reflects it under the ceiling, clip sets it to the ceiling, bypass passes it
Sets the voltage below which the floor mode acts, -10V to 10V, with gain and offset applied to it as well as to the signal; a cable at the floor level input replaces it
Sets the voltage above which the ceiling mode acts, -10V to 10V, with gain and offset applied to it as well as to the signal; a cable at the ceiling level input replaces it
Transposes the scale in semitones, -12 to 12, carrying every note's priority with it, so the key changes and the mode does not
Moves the priorities round the notes already in the scale without adding any, so the mode changes and the key does not; a setting that lands on no note of the scale changes nothing
The voltage to be processed and quantized; with nothing patched, one channel of white noise between -10V and 10V is used, and the channels patched here are the channels every output carries
Sets the gain in place of the knob while patched, its voltage divided by 10 and multiplied by the knob, so the knob attenuates it
Sets the offset in place of the knob while patched, its voltage added straight to the signal; the knob does not attenuate it, despite the maker's tooltip saying that it does
Takes a new sample of the input on each rising edge, and clocks the shift register as well while the clock input is empty
Steps the shift register on each rising edge; with nothing patched here the s&h input does that instead
Writes the input into the current step of the shift register on the next clock while this reads 1V or above, in place of playing that step back
Chooses the floor mode in place of the knob while patched, its voltage cut to a whole number, 0 for to ceiling through to 4 for bypass
Chooses the ceiling mode in place of the knob while patched, its voltage cut to a whole number, 0 for to root through to 4 for bypass
Sets the floor in place of the knob while patched, -10V to 10V before gain and offset are applied to it
Sets the ceiling in place of the knob while patched, -10V to 10V before gain and offset are applied to it
Sets the transposition in place of the knob while patched, at 1V per octave, wrapping round every twelve semitones
Sets the priority shift in place of the knob while patched, at 1V per octave; a voltage that rounds to a note outside the scale leaves the shift where it was
The input after sample and hold, the loop, gain, offset and the floor and ceiling limits, with no quantizing applied
The processed input quantized to every note of the scale that is not black; the prio shift control makes no difference here, because this output takes any note above black whatever its priority
The processed input quantized to the notes of the scale set to mid grey, light grey or white
The processed input quantized to the notes of the scale set to light grey or white
The processed input quantized to the notes of the scale set to white
Note — the input runs through sample and hold, then the sixteen-step shift register, then gain, then offset, then the floor and ceiling limits, and only then the quantizer
Note — a value is quantized down to the nearest scale note at or below it, not to whichever scale note is closest
Note — the root that the ceiling's to root mode uses is the lowest note in the scale whose priority is below white, not the lowest white note the manual describes
Note — the twelve coloured dots by the keyboard show each note's priority after transpose and prio shift have been applied; they are drawing only and no click reaches them
Note — the contents of the shift register are saved with the patch and come back on reload, so a loop survives a restart
melody_transformer.notes: Written from the maker's source at commit 7f2d7f2 (the plugin.json carrying 2.0.1); head carries the same source. Three places where the code and the README disagree, and the code is what shipped. First, the offset input's tooltip says '-10 to 10v, attenuverted by knob' but line 334 substitutes the jack voltage for the knob without multiplying by it; the gain input's identical wording is correct, because line 332 does multiply. Second, the README defines the root note as the lowest note with priority 4, the white one; line 293 takes the lowest note whose priority is below 3, which on the shipped default scale is F rather than C, and that is the note the ceiling's to root mode uses. Third, the README describes the default scale as root at prio4, root and fifth at prio3 and a triad at prio2, then says the maker might change it; the shipped defaults are C=4, E=3, G=3, D=2, A=2, F=1, B=1, which is the revised configuration he describes at the end of that section - root, triad, pentatonic, whole scale. getQuantizedValue() dereferences the iterator it lands on without checking the list is non-empty, so setting every note to black leaves all four priority lists empty and the four quantized outputs reading past the end of an empty vector. The twelve note buttons, the gain, offset, floor and ceiling knobs and the transpose and prio shift knobs are all configured with empty names, so those tooltips are blank. The mode CV inputs clamp to 0 to 5 while the switches only define 0 to 4, so a 5V reading falls through every case and behaves as bypass.
